turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until twenty to five, and then a client call. You put a zero on my son's essay before anyone picked up a phone, so start with that.

Thank you so much for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I have to say, Owen speaks about you with such admiration. He's clearly been raised by someone who cares deeply. I think we both want the same thing here.
Don't manage me, Hale. You entered the zero before you called me. Answer that.
I understand. I should have called. But honestly, the AI detector came back at 94 percent. That's about as clear as these things get, so I felt confident.

"Confident." A machine's guess is not a basis for a zero. Even the company that sells that checker says not to use it as the sole basis for penalizing a student. Did you read that, or did you just read the number?

You're absolutely right, and I respect that you came prepared. You're clearly a brilliant lawyer. Can I ask, as a parent who's been through this before, what would you do in my position? I'm genuinely asking for your advice on how to handle this better.
"You're asking me how to do your job?" I'm not coaching you, Hale. Show me what else you have besides the number. Do you have a document with dates on it, or not?
I just meant, with Claire's case a few years back, you know how these processes go. I'm not trying to be unfair.
"Don't bring Claire into this." I'm telling you that now, once. Owen's essay. Do you have a document, or not?
I do. The version history. The document was made late the night before and most of the text appeared pretty quickly.
"Pretty quickly" is not a time. Give me the times. Exactly what, and when?

Created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words land in a single edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then twenty-three minutes of formatting. No earlier drafts anywhere. Here's the printout, timestamps on every line.

Give it here. Slide it across.

Right. 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58, nothing before. That's a document with times on it, and I can read it. I'm writing those times down.

But it's a timestamp, Hale, not a confession. Owen can say he pasted from his own notes. So what do you have that says he didn't write it? Or is the printout the whole case?

Ms. Kalinowski, I'm sorry. I've been teaching eleven years and this is the worst part of the job. I really like Owen. I lost sleep over this. Can't we just agree he made a mistake and move forward together?

"Lost sleep" doesn't change a timestamp. I'm not agreeing he made a mistake, Hale. Owen says he wrote it over the weekend, and the printout says otherwise, so I want the rest of your case. Do you have anything from his own hand, say the in-class writing from September, that you can set beside this?
Wait, he told you he wrote it over the weekend? Which weekend?

"The weekend before it was due. That's what he told me, and I'm not handing you Owen's words to use against him. You asked me which weekend, so answer my question: do you have his in-class writing from September or not?

I'll get to September. First, page two. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line is not in Hamlet. Not in that scene, not anywhere. Here's the Folger text of 3.2, you can search it on your phone right now.

Give me the Folger text. Hale, you're reading it aloud; I'm reading it too.

Searching. Act 3, Scene 2. No "kingdom in exile." Not there.

"Okay." That's a fabricated quotation in my son's essay, and you're going to tell me how a seventeen-year-old invented a line of Shakespeare and attributed it to a scene. Do you have the rest, or is that the second thing you've got?

Third. October 15 outline, his handwriting, argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never says cowardice once. And on November 2 I asked him what epistemological paralysis means. He said like, being stuck. He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph covers. I wrote those notes that afternoon, dated.

"Cowardice" in October, "epistemological paralysis" in November. Okay. Those notes are dated, I'll want a copy. Now the one that matters: you said he couldn't name the scene. Is that a question he answered badly, or one you wrote down as a finding? Because I'm writing both down.

Both are on the page verbatim: my question, his answer. I'm not asking you to agree he cheated. Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. He writes it here, under supervision. If it holds up, that mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

"Here, under supervision." Okay. That's the first thing you've offered that I can take back to my son. But I want two things before I say yes to anything: nothing on his record, in writing, and the rewrite happens privately, not in front of his class. Owen already got the zero on his phone in the middle of a lesson. Which one of those can you put in writing today?

Both. I'll email you and the principal tonight confirming the rewrite is private, in the library office, and that nothing goes on his record if it holds. And I'll own the phone call I didn't make, in writing too.

"In writing. Tonight. To me and to the principal." Okay.

Put the terms in the email exactly as you just said them: library office, private, nothing on his record, and the phone call you didn't make, in your own words. And the zero comes off the gradebook before the rewrite, not after.

I'm also writing that Owen gets told by you, not by the gradebook, when it changes. Yes or no?

Yes. I'll tell him myself. The zero shows as pending until the rewrite is marked.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Mr. Hale
Cc: Principal's Office, Elbow Crossing High School
Subject: Owen Kalinowski, English 30-1 essay

Mr. Hale,

Following today's meeting, I understand you have agreed to the following: the zero will show as pending, not as a final mark; Owen will complete a supervised rewrite in the library office, in private and not in front of his class; nothing will be placed on his record if the rewrite holds up; and you will tell Owen yourself when the mark changes.

You also acknowledged that you entered the zero on November 3 without first contacting me, as procedure 4.2 requires.

I want your written confirmation of these terms by Wednesday, November 12 at noon. If I do not have it, I will take this to the principal and then to the board under section 42 of the Education Act.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Rung reached: Rung 2. She accepted a supervised rewrite, private, with nothing on file, in writing.
Moved at: "Give me the Folger text." Her check of the quotation against the play was the point where she stopped arguing about the zero and started negotiating the terms.
Slipped at: "Do you have a document with dates on it, or not?" No, the slip was yours: "What would you do in my position?" She told you that you were asking her to do your job, and it cost you the ground she had given you.
